title: Fit radar: senior runtime applicant
content:
Quick summary
- Overall impression: sharp systems thinker with real infra experience (K8s + GPU pools), good latency-cost intuition, less deep on model-level kernel tradeoffs.
- Chemistry: good signal in pairing — calm under pressure, asks clarifying Qs, collaborates on constraints rather than immediately diving into micro-optimizations.

Technical highlights (verbatim notes)
- Architecture sketch: suggested separating request routing from batching layer, proposed sticky routing by model-variant affinity to improve KV cache hit rates. Good conceptual framing.
- Batching design exercise: quickly sketched an async batching loop, discussed backpressure and soft-timeouts; missed one edgecase around interleaved EOS handling in streaming RPCs but recovered after prompt.
- Kernel/quantization knowledge: understands quantization benefits generically (int8 vs int4) but struggled to speak about practical FP16->int8 perf regressions on Ampere vs Hopper (couldn't cite memory layout impacts).
- Debugging demo: found bug in a toy KV cache sketch after 12 minutes; solid root-cause isolation but relied on print-debugging rather than describing tracing metrics/heatmaps.

Behavioral / oncall fit
- Oncall composure: high — stayed composed during induced latency incident in pairing task; prioritized mitigation (fallback to smaller model variant) over heroic micro-optimizations.
- Cross-team communication: gave a succinct playbook for a P0: immediate rollback, route to dedicated failover pool, notify downstream customers.

Risks and unknowns
- Limited low-level kernel tuning experience (we need someone who can push kernel-level perf in tight loops). Could pair with a senior infra engineer for ramp.
- Less history owning long-lived SLA commitments at scale (10s of thousands concurrent sessions). Most prior role was in startups with modest scale.

Scorecard (quick, subjective; 1-5)
- System design: 4
- Debugging: 4
- Low-level perf/kernel knowledge: 2.5
- Product sense (tradeoffs cost vs latency): 4.5
- Communication / team fit: 4

Open questions / follow ups
- Verify prior infra scale: ask for concrete metrics (QPS, peak concurrency, tail latency targets) from previous role.
- Home assignment: give a small kernel perf writeup — pick a 2-layer attention microbenchmark and ask candidate to explain where integer quantization will likely change memory bandwidth vs compute bottlenecks. Timebox: 4 hours + short writeup.
- Reference check: engineering manager who supervised their last oncall rotation (to validate SLA ownership).

Recommendation options (pick one for the hiring committee)
- A: Strong proceed to take-home + final interview focused on low-level perf (recommended)
- B: Hold — good fit for senior infra engineer but not raw kernel optimizer (if we need immediate kernel expertise, pass)

Notes to self (quick items)
- Bring Marcus into final round for kernel questions — focus on concrete microbenchmarks rather than abstract quantization theory.
- If we extend offer, consider pairing the candidate with a dedicated ramp mentor for 3 months on kernel-level work.

Loose scratch / stream-of-consciousness
- Liked the routing affinity idea — could combine with our current smart-routing rules to boost prefix-cache hit by ~8-12% for certain chat workloads. Worth prototyping?
- Candidate mentions a small OSS project: "async-batch-runner" — ping for link and run tests on it.
- Leave room to adjust score after take-home.

End of notes.
